headline: Math is nearly solved; agents doing real work remain the gap
outlook: Math is where the headroom has nearly run out. Over the last twelve months the field closed 95% of the remaining gap there, FrontierMath crossed 90% in September, and GPT-6.1 Sol has now posted 100% on FrontierMath Tier 4. Agents and real work are moving far more slowly, with only 34% of headroom closed over the year, the Remote Labor Index at 20.8% and OSWorld 2 at 31.4%, even though APEX-Agents jumped from 68.6% to 82.2% across three records in late September. The link between those two pictures is task length: the longest task horizon is 17.4 hours with Claude Mythos Preview and has been doubling roughly every 4.1 months, which on current trends puts a full 40-hour work-week most likely around December 2026, with a plausible range running to August 2027. Meanwhile, the price of reaching 80% on GPQA has fallen from $3.44 per million tokens with Gemini 2.5 Pro in March 2025 to $0.055 with Qwen3.7 Flash, and it is dropping about 21× a year, so whatever these agents can do is getting cheap quickly; still, treat the dates loosely, since past likely ranges caught the real outcome only 59% of the time, and Terminal-Bench and GeoBench show how the last few points can stall well behind schedule.
